title: Acoustic fluctuations of two-dimensional dipolar supersolids
abstract: We investigate the microscopic structure of the long-wavelength acoustic excitations of two-dimensional dipolar supersolids with triangular and honeycomb crystal order. Using Bogoliubov--de Gennes calculations, we determine the density, phase, current, and lattice-displacement fluctuations associated with the three acoustic modes. We develop a procedure to extract the lattice displacement directly from the microscopic density perturbation, allowing the modes to be identified as one transverse and two longitudinal branches. The displacement field further separates the density fluctuations into contributions from crystal strain and particle transport relative to the lattice. This reveals that the lower longitudinal mode can have large strain and defect-density fluctuations that substantially cancel in the total density response. We show that the long-wavelength fluctuation amplitudes agree with hydrodynamic theory, which is specified entirely by the elastic coefficients of the supersolid. Our analysis provides a microscopic connection between Bogoliubov excitations and the crystalline and superfluid degrees of freedom of two-dimensional supersolids, and identifies their signatures in density- and current-sensitive probes.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes sound wave excitations in 2D dipolar supersolids using Bogoliubov-de Gennes theory. It decomposes density fluctuations into contributions from crystal strain and particle transport, identifying three distinct acoustic modes. The results confirm that the microscopic quantum description correctly reproduces macroscopic hydrodynamic predictions based on elastic constants.
main_problem: The study investigates the microscopic structure of long-wavelength acoustic excitations in two-dimensional dipolar supersolids.
main_result: The analysis successfully connects Bogoliubov excitation modes to measurable crystalline and superfluid degrees of freedom, showing that fluctuation amplitudes match hydrodynamic theory based on elastic coefficients.
method: Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) calculations are used to determine quasiparticle excitations, followed by developing a procedure to extract the lattice displacement field from density perturbations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a two-dimensional dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate exhibiting crystalline order (triangular or honeycomb). The dynamics are analyzed using linearizations of the extended Gross–Pitaevskii equation.
key_observables: Density ($\varrho$), phase ($\vartheta$), current ($J$), and lattice displacement fluctuations associated with three acoustic modes (one transverse, two longitudinal).
important_parameters: Long-wavelength limit ($|q|a \ll 1$); zero temperature; elastic coefficients of the supersolid.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a uniform planar geometry and focuses on small distortions relative to the lattice constant.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the three acoustic modes, phase diagrams showing triangular/honeycomb states, and spectra detailing density, strain, and defect density fluctuations for different excitation bands.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system and governing equations (eGPE/BdG) to analyzing specific fluctuation components ($\delta	ilde{ho}, \delta	ilde{ho}_u, \delta	ilde{ho}_\Delta$) for each acoustic mode, culminating in comparisons with established hydrodynamic sum rules.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed microscopic link between the quantum excitation spectrum (BdG) and macroscopic continuum properties (elasticity/hydrodynamics) in exotic quantum matter like supersolids, which is highly relevant to modern AMO research.
